paper_sections.title: Arithmetic in two languages: Localizing simple multiplication processing in the adult bilingual brain

description.value: The study investigated whether simple multiplication processing differs between the language in which bilingual adults learned multiplication and their other language, using behavioral measures and fMRI.

spans.text: For question 1, we compared the languages collapsed across problem size

design.value: Within-subject bilingual fMRI study with two languages, two problem-size conditions, true and false multiplication solutions, localizer tasks, behavioral analyses, ROI analyses, whole-brain exploratory analyses, hierarchical regressions, and Bayesian modeling.

spans.text: Participants performed two localizer tasks (verbal and numerosity) and the experimental task (single-digit multiplication verification) in a single experimental session.
Participants were right-handed (assessed by the Edinburgh Inventory, Oldfield, 1971 ; range: 0.35-1.00)
